description:
Making Chocolate Ice Cream is one of the hardest "simple" ice creams to make. So many things can go wrong when making chocolate ice cream so we decided to start a mini series to help get through the basic elements and try and stop your chocolate ice cream from going wrong. 

In this video, we talk about how chocolate effects your ice cream and what can happen if you don't balance your recipes properly. 
Unfortuntely, there are so many ice cream recipes on the internet that are too low in sugars, too high in fats, generally just bad recipes too and that's before we even go in to the no churn recipes (i'll do another video about the no churn era).

We look at why all chocolate and cocoas powders are different and also how to make sure your new ice cream recipe turns out the best possible. 

We need to remember that ice cream (like all things) can be different for eveyone. Some like low sugar, some high fat (me) and some with other desires. If you follow this channel, we make retail grade ice cream, using a home ice cream machine. The machine is a Musso 5030 Stella, all our recipes will work with any home grade machine so you don't have to worry.

Would you like us to do a video on No Churn Ice Cream? Let us know in the comments!
Would you like to see more Vegan ice cream recipes? Let us know in the comments!

Great video Nick!  We roast our own cacao beans and make bean to bar chocolate. 100% is used when added to our mix. We also produce our own cacao butter and the byproduct is cacao powder, also without sugar. Depending on the bean we use will depend on the fat content as each bean is different and because the cacao butter is squeezed from the chocolate mass, the powder has very  little fat content left.  I do use the same balancing calc as you mentioned but always guessing when it comes time to add percentages of chocolate and powder.  Any thoughts?
Thanks
